entries.reason: This paper proposes a chemical symbiosis strategy to design a dual-phase halide electrolyte integrating nanocrystalline LiAlCl4 with amorphous Li-M-O-Cl (M = Ta/Al) phases, which synergistically combines the ultra-high-voltage stability (up to 4.8 V) of the crystalline phase with the low-energy-barrier ion transport pathways in the amorphous matrix.
entries.title: High-Voltage Solid-State Batteries That Work in Extreme Temperatures
entries.paragraph: Researchers have developed a new type of solid-state battery that can operate at high voltages and extreme temperatures, from -60°C to 55°C. The battery uses a dual-phase halide solid electrolyte that combines the stability of a crystalline phase with the conductivity of an amorphous matrix. This innovative design enables the battery to retain 90.5% of its capacity after 100 cycles at 4.8V and maintain a specific capacity of 133 mA h g-1 over 500 cycles at 55°C and 3C.

entries.reason: This paper introduces a new class of solid state capacitive batteries that store energy in structured electric fields rather than chemical bonds, addressing the next major bottleneck in global electrification: scalable, safe, fast charging, high density energy storage without dependence on lithium or faradaic chemistry.
entries.title: A New Class of Solid-State Batteries That Store Energy in Electric Fields
entries.paragraph: Scientists have introduced a new class of solid-state batteries that store energy in structured electric fields rather than chemical bonds. This approach eliminates the need for lithium or faradaic chemistry and enables fast charging, high-density energy storage, and scalability. The researchers have developed three engineered architectures for these batteries, including doped semiconductor parallel plate cells, multilayer PCB-style stacked capacitive banks, and hybrid N/P doped dielectric fusion cells.

entries.reason: This paper investigates amorphous titanium tetrasulfide (TiS4) as a high-capacity cathode material for sulfide-based solid-state batteries using Li6PS5Cl argyrodite as solid electrolyte, and reveals that tribochemical processing intensity determines composite microstructure and electrochemical performance.
entries.title: Improving Solid-State Batteries with Tribochemical Interface Engineering
entries.paragraph: Researchers have investigated the use of amorphous titanium tetrasulfide (TiS4) as a high-capacity cathode material for sulfide-based solid-state batteries. They found that high-energy ball milling (HBM) processing intensity determines the composite microstructure and electrochemical performance. HBM-processed composites exhibit superior homogenization and achieve discharge capacities of 1110 mAh g S-1 at 0.05C and 669 mAh g S-1 at 0.5C.

entries.reason: This paper demonstrates a high-entropy design strategy by substituting the P-site in Li6PS5I with Ge, Sb, Si, and As, yielding Li6.5As0.25Si0.25Ge0.25Sb0.25S5I with a configurational entropy of 2.04R, which increases structural (occupational) disorder and facilitates lithium transport.
entries.title: High-Entropy Design for Improved Ionic Conductivity and Air Stability
entries.paragraph: Scientists have developed a high-entropy design strategy to improve the ionic conductivity and air stability of lithium argyrodites. By substituting the P-site in Li6PS5I with Ge, Sb, Si, and As, they created a material with a configurational entropy of 2.04R. The resulting material exhibits room-temperature ionic conductivities of 8.0 mS cm-1 in a cold-pressed state and 11.4 mS cm-1 for hot-pressed pellets.

entries.reason: This paper proposes a Dual-Extended Kalman Filter (DEKF) framework for joint estimation of state of charge (SOC) and state of temperature (SOT) in solid-state lithium-ion batteries, which poses challenges for accurately estimating battery state in battery management systems.
entries.title: Accurate State Estimation for Solid-State Batteries
entries.paragraph: Researchers have proposed a Dual-Extended Kalman Filter (DEKF) framework for joint estimation of state of charge (SOC) and state of temperature (SOT) in solid-state lithium-ion batteries. They established a second-order equivalent circuit model and a two-state thermal model, and designed a DEKF-based estimator to simultaneously estimate SOC, surface temperature, and core temperature. Validation under four typical dynamic driving cycles showed accurate SOC and temperature estimation.
